title: The city becomes a sequence of rooms
governingQuestion: How does Milan turn heritage architecture into temporary fashion infrastructure?
status: evidence-backed draft; recording, named interviews and owner-final approval remain open

longform.headline: The city becomes a sequence of rooms
longform.opening: Milan does not have one runway; it has rooms carrying centuries into temporary use.

sections.heading: Then
sections.copy: CNMI’s Fashion Hub uses Palazzo Giureconsulti as a meeting and presentation site for selected emerging designers.

sections.heading: Now
sections.copy: The official calendar coordinates shows, presentations and digital events across Milan rather than specifying one permanent runway venue.

sections.heading: Next—and the limit
sections.copy: Room-level lighting, sound, power, accessibility and supplier specifications remain event-by-event reporting assignments.

longform.closing: Milan’s technology is not futurist decoration. It is the system that moves authority from name to room to object to record.
